title: The goddess within
hookLine: a jeweled city far away, and then the hymn gives the goddess a home in the body
carry: the body is the goddess's home too
tomorrow: near enough to love, and without form. both?

lines: AN OCEAN OF NECTAR, A HOUSE OF GEMS.
cards: Same goddess, two addresses. Early in the Lalita Sahasranama she lives somewhere grand.
The names place her in the middle of an ocean of nectar, in a forest of kadamba trees, in a house of wish-granting gems, seated on a throne. A palace you'd need a map to find.
Then, further on, the hymn turns and gives her a second address, and this one isn't far away at all. It's a human body, starting at the base of the spine.

teach.h: FROM THE ROOT OF THE SPINE.
teach.b: Here is the run, in paraphrase, and it moves like a climb. Her one dwelling is the muladhara, the root center at the base of the spine. She pierces the knot of Brahma.
She rises within the manipura, the center at the navel. She pierces the knot of Vishnu. She stands within the ajna, the center between the brows.
She pierces the knot of Rudra. She rises onto the thousand-petaled lotus at the crown of the head, and from there she pours down streams of nectar.
A few names on, the hymn calls her bright as a streak of lightning, dwelling above the six centers, and names her outright: Kundalini, the coiled one, fine as the thread inside a lotus stalk.
So the queen of the jeweled city is also a power curled at the root of a human body, rising, untying knots and raining nectar back down.

teach.h: TO THE LOTUS AT THE CROWN.
teach.b: In Shakta Tantra and in the Sri Vidya tradition these names are read as a map for inner practice, and those practices are taught by a teacher, in person, with care. This path doesn't teach them.

Others hear the names devotionally: the goddess isn't only out there. And here's the teaching under both, one Tantra says loudest: the body isn't a cage the spirit puts up with. It's where the goddess lives.
Kundalini isn't a gym word; it's her name.

teach.h: THE BODY IS HER HOME TOO.
teach.b: So the way you sleep, eat and sit can count as care for a home of the divine.

how: In Shakta Tantra and the Sri Vidya tradition, the kundalini names of the Lalita Sahasranama are read as a map of inner practice taught by a guru; other devotees simply recite them as praise of the goddess within.

o: a yoga manual for raising energy up the spine
a hymn of names placing the goddess in the body too
a map of the jeweled city where Lalita lives

games.q: a second address: tap the pairs.
p: the root center, base of the spine
at the crown of the head

s: in the hymn, the goddess lives only in a faraway jeweled city
a run of names also places her in the body, rising from the root of the spine.
the three knots she pierces carry the names of Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra
she pierces each in turn on the way up.
the hymn ends the climb at the crown and stops there
from the crown she pours down streams of nectar.

games.q: you've climbed with the names from the root of the spine to the lotus at the crown. what does the goddess do next, in the hymn?
games.why: the name after the crown says she pours down streams of nectar: the climb ends in something given back.

practice: Sit tall without strain and feel where you meet the chair or the floor, the base of the spine, solid and supported; then let attention move slowly to the belly rising and falling, to the space between the brows, to the crown of the head.

No pushing, no picturing energy, just noticing, place by place, the way you'd walk up a staircase in your own house. If you pray, you can greet the goddess at each step; if you don't, let the climb be quiet.

wordCard.voice: The Lalita Sahasranama. Today, the names that give the goddess a second home: rising from the root of the spine to the lotus at the crown.

orig.note: Sanskrit kuṇḍalinī: 'the coiled one,' a name the hymn gives the goddess as the power at the root of the spine.

carryVoice: Your line: the body is the goddess's home too. Kundalini is her name. Same time tomorrow.
